notes: Account profile: mid-size health system with integrated ambulatory network + specialty clinics.
Use-case priority: clinician-facing search (fast retrieval during consult) > patient-facing summarization later.
Data characteristics: average note 700-1,200 tokens; high duplication across templates; many small incremental updates.
Index scale: expect 25-40M documents, ~200M vectors after chunking (policy: 250-300 token chunks).
Performance ask: <200ms p95 for answers on reranked results; 50-80ms p95 for dense-only lookups (cached).
Cost sensitivity: finance wants modeled costs for 12 QPS steady-state and bursts; target <$0.03/query after committed capacity.
Security: Must keep PHI in customer-controlled network. No public internet egress for raw PHI. Full audit trail per access and per-token logging required.
Integration: Epic/CareConnect is primary EHR — Epic security team needs network diagram + signed BA before connector tests.
Quote from Dr Khatri: 'We need instant, trustworthy answers in the chart; false positives are risky.'
POC success criteria: 1) p95 latency <=200ms for clinician workflow, 2) reranker F1 improvement > 18% over BM25 baseline on internal eval set, 3) validated audit logs & key management flow.
SE notes: consider quantized models for reranker, prefix KV caching for common queries, and aggressive shard-locality for hot-patient records.
Procurement note: Legal asked for standard Redwood SOC2 + ISO documentation and an outline of Private deployment topology.
Internal: potential upsell to Redwood Optimize for automated batching/tuning and to Dedicated reserved pools for predictable SLA.
sales_tldr: Enterprise health system evaluating Redwood Private/Dedicated for PHI-safe RAG search. POC running on de-identified subset; main risks are Epic connector sign-off and PHI data transfer approvals. Strong chance if POC meets latency/cost targets and security attestation provided.
